	public static URL open(URL host) throws Exception {

		String hostUrl = host.toString();
		String validChars = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789._-";

		String cleanUrl = "";

		for (int i = 0; i < hostUrl.length(); i++) {

				cleanUrl = cleanUrl + String.valueOf(hostUrl.charAt(i));

				cleanUrl = cleanUrl + " ";
			}
		}

}# Web App Killer

An online web application to validate your code for competitions such as Coding Competition, Google Code Jam, ACM-ICPC, etc. See more here: [coding-competitions.com](https://www.coding-competitions.com/)

## Getting Started

Clone or download repository.

```
$ git clone https://github.com/jiminhuang126/web-app-killer.git
```

Make sure have npm installed or just download npm from [npmjs.com](https://www.npmjs.com/get-npm).

```
$ cd web-app-killer
$ npm install
```

## Usage
Run these commands to get the development environment running.

```
$ npm run build-css
$ npm start <PORT>
```

    public static String getUrlContent(String url) {
        String host = url;

        // Remove space-related characters from url
        for (int i = host.length(); i > 0; i--) {
            try {
                boolean isNotValidChar =!Character.isJavaIdentifierPart(host.charAt(i - 1));

                if (isNotValidChar) {
                    host = host.substring(0, i - 1);
                }
            } catch (StringIndexOutOfBoundsException e) {
                break;
            }

            // Stop removing when the string is clean
            if (host.length() == 0) {
                break;
            }
        }

        URL urlObject = new URL(host);
        return urlObject.openStream().toString();

This repository contains resources for CS201 on 2023. It contains a list of slides containing CS201 lectures that were taught on the  course-wide virtual platform, Code230, and exercises that were taught on Code215. Each CS201 lecture contains a separate folder.

## Structure
Each lecture’s folder contains all slides for that lecture, the corresponding exercises, and, optionally, a video recording of the lecture.

To navigate through this folder, run `cd` in a terminal and type in the lecture’s folder name (e.g., `CD3.1`) at this path: `cs201-2023` 
If you’re using Mac or Linux, you can use your terminal’s tab completion to navigate through the folders. If you’re using Windows, you’ll need to change the folder path to match what you’re using.

Inside each folder, you will find the following files:
1. `Lectures.txt`: A text file that contains every lecture in that folder (useful for navigation).
2. `Exercises.txt`: A text file with the names of all exercises.
3. `Exercises`, a folder containing each exercise's folder.
4. `Exercises.pdf`, the PDF of all the exercises.

In this repository, you may find the following resources useful:

3. `Lectures`: A zip file with the slides for all CS201 lectures

    public static void unzip(String archName, String dest)
        throws Exception {
        if (archName == null || archName.isEmpty()) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Wrong parameter for archName");
        }
        FileInputStream input = new FileInputStream(archName);
        ZipInputStream zip = new ZipInputStream(input);
		
        ZipEntry entry;
        while ((entry = zip.getNextEntry())!= null) {
            // проверяваме дали името на члена не съдържа '..', ако е така
            // предотвратяваме прехода по 'dest' с допълнителни
            // директории
            if (entry.getName().indexOf("..") == -1) {
				File destEntry = new File(dest, entry.getName());
				
                // ако при извършване на unzip се е намерила директория,
                // създаваме нея. Ако няма директория (файл), създаваме
                // файла за запис.
                if (destEntry.isDirectory()) {
                    destEntry.mkdirs();
                    // разминаваме файловата система
                    continue;
                } else {
                    FileOutputStream output = new FileOutputStream(destEntry);
                    byte[] buffer = new byte[1024];
                    int len;
                    while ((len = zip.read(buffer)) > 0) {
                        output.write(buffer, 0, len);
                    }
                    output.close();
                }
            }
        }
        zip.close();
        
    }

        int i = zip.read(bytes, 0, bytes.length);
        while (i!= -1) {
            fout.write(bytes, 0, i);
            i = zip.read(bytes, 0, bytes.length);
        }

# CTF Training System

Online training system with interactive exercises for competitions [DEF CON CTF](https://ctftime.org/event/225) and derivatives.

## Components

* CTF training system UI and game engine.
* Backend web server (for game engine API and for challenge description extraction services).
* Challenge description extractor (based on Java source code analysis).
* Exercises database.

## Installation

1. Make sure Java is installed (e.g. via [OpenJDK](https://openjdk.java.net/) or [Oracle Java](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/javase-downloads.html)).

2. Change `docker-compose.yml` to reflect the desired location for the data volumes. Data will be stored in the `./data` subdir of the repository.

   ```yaml
   volumes:
     - data:/data
   ```

3. Run `docker-compose up -d` to start the CTF training system.

## Usage

The CTF training system is accessible at `http://localhost:8080`.

## Configuration

All configuration files are located in `/configs` and are mounted into the environment. For example, database configuration for H2 in `/configs/db.properties`:

```properties
db_user=user
db_pass=
db_url=jdbc:h2:./data/ctf-training-system
```

In this problem, you will write a program that evaluates reverse polish notation (RPN) expressions, which are similar to infix notation (e.g., x + y).
Recall that RPN involves parsing expressions in a postfix form and evaluating the expression by means of a stack that may contain operators (+, -, /, \*) and values (3, 7). The last operation (leftmost) in the expression determines which operation is performed. For example, the expression ( 3 + 5 ) * 2 can be written 3 5 + 2 *. If your program encounters an operator, it pops two values from the stack, evaluates the operation, and then pushes the result back onto the top of stack. Operators are the only element which cause the value popping and evaluation. Thus, their order corresponds to the precedence of the operations.

### 401 - Bad Request

A server can return a `401 Unauthorized` response to any of the following:

- An HTML page containing a login form.
- A redirect response to a login form page.
- An HTML page using forms that ask the user’s credentials.
- An HTML page giving an interactive form that will prompt the user for authentication.
- A redirect response that uses a web form.

An HTTP 401 status is reserved for responses returned when a client fails to provide authentication information.

A client is required to provide credentials in the form described for each of the following cases.

- A browser client submits a form to a server that requires a browser session for authentication.
- A web client submits a form to a server that requires a browser session for authentication.
- A program client uses forms on a web server that requires authentication.
- A program that sends a web request to a web server using a browser-independent protocol (HTTP) like `wget`.

## Server response

A server can return the following information as part of the HTTP response:

- A textual response explaining what went wrong (the *error message*).
- The requested content that identifies the problem, such as a page that explains the error to the user.

## Authentication

When an authentication mechanism is required, the server can return either a login form that presents the user with the credentials to supply or any other method to retrieve credentials.

Examples of authentication methods include HTTP GET parameters, an HTML form, or a browser-specific authentication scheme (`BASIC` or `DIGEST`).

A Java based language trainer designed for Java novices.
Written by  (aka EduZhang) for a school assignment in 2016 and reworked and expanded in late 2016.

![Screenshot of the start menu](https://github.com/EduZhang/MisterExpert/blob/master/screenshots/start.jpg)


## A Short Introduction
The program consists of two main components:

1. The trainer.
2. The assistance.

When you run the program from CMD, you start the trainer.
In addition to the program itself, there are two additional programs created by EduZhang to make training more interesting.
When you run the trainer first, you will be prompted to download the assistance program.
The assistance program helps you while you are in the training mode.
The assistance program, written in Python, can be executed by typing "Python Assist.py".
You can now start the trainer, and the program will prompt you to download the Python file.

If you have the Python program on your system, you can use the program in the training mode, and the assistance will be activated.
You will see some helpful functions, such as the Ping class, that is similar to a Windows program. In this context, the Ping is the program in the assistance mode. When you use the Ping, you can ping a host and see what pings back. The Ping program can only be used in the training mode. To download this program, simply write down the following Python program in your CMD terminal and type it in. You will also need to download the Python program yourself if you don’t have one.

# Code Generation

Source code is a programming language that is easier to understand, but the computer has to understand something called `byte code`. This step translates the code into what the computer does when it runs it.

If you try to compile the following, you will see that it only allows code that is translated in a single byte for the byte code, like the `char` type:

There are two types of Java source code: `1.4` and `8`. Java 1.4 is used when you are writing code for Java 1.4 environments and Java 8 when you are writing code for Java 8 environments. The type of Java source code is indicated using a comment `/** @version 8 */`.

If you do not put this comment, there is a slight chance that the code will compile successfully for Java 8 environments or the version of Java that you use. However, it is safe and correct to use the Java language version comment in `1.4` source files because all the Java 1.4 versions can accept `1.4` source files. That is why the code provided here is written for Java 8 when you create `1.4` source files.

import java.time.LocalDateTime;
import java.util.Comparator;

public class MyComparator implements Comparator<String> {

    private String field;

    public MyComparator(String field) {
        this.field = field;
    }

    @Override
    public int compare(String object1, String object2) {
        LocalDateTime time1 = LocalDateTime.parse(object1.substring(field.length() + 1));
        LocalDateTime time2 = LocalDateTime.parse(object2.substring(field.length() + 1));
        if (time1.isBefore(time2))
            return -1;
        else if (time1.isAfter(time2))
            return 1;
        return 0;
    }
}

# Rendering Jinja2 tags

Jinja2 and its extensions have a way to mark HTML content with
additional meaning. The best known such marker is `{{... ||}}`.
A typical example is the use of an image within a link, as seen in:

```
[link](/to/the/wiki)
![Image](content_for_image)
```

The following code shows two possible implementations for the
rendering of such tags:

```
{{ content ||}}.

{{ content | htmlsafe }}.
```

Which way is clearer?

When in doubt, always use the less specific version.

# Output from a pipeline

Some programs take the output of one command as input for another.
For example, a grep runs against a certain text file,
and the output is matched to pattern.
In some cases the input can also be an output of a program:
If a program takes plain text input, but its output is another file that can be
used as input, it's called *an input pipe*.

Together with the command line of the previous exercise,
a file can be used as input to the `grep` command, so the output text
is matched to a certain pattern.

In this exercise, the `grep` command is introduced first using a
file as input. After that, the input can be an output of other
programs. The `grep` command is then used to find
the output from the input of `tail`:
The output from `tail` contains text from the end of the file that
was printed out. With `grep`, these lines are searched for the given
pattern.

### Example 2: Use an existing function to bypass validation logic
If we know where the function is used and we suspect that it is calling other functions, we can look within those functions to find where the validation logic can be bypassed. For example, we know that the `execute()` function in [db](https://github.com/owasp/go-top10/blob/1.2/OWASP%20Top%2010%202021%20Project/11_Untrusted_Code_Execution/python/07_db_and_nosql/src/db.py) is being used to get user input.

We can look within that function and find the call to `db.execute()` like this:
```python
# A function that takes user input, stores it, and performs an SQL query on it
def set_input(form_input, new_input):
    userInput = ""
    userInput = form_input
    sqlStr = f"UPDATE person SET {new_input}='{userInput}' WHERE id=1 AND password=''"
    # SQL query to update user input information on database
    db.execute(sqlStr)
    print(f"{new_input} is now: {userInput}")
    
# Function that allows us to input data on the database
def input_data(field):
    newData = ""
    newData = input(f"Please enter new {field}: ")
    field = field
    set_input(newData, field)
    
input_data()
```

We can find the SQL injection in the second line of code:
```python
sqlStr = f"UPDATE person SET {new_input}='{userInput}' WHERE id=1 AND password=''"
```

First, we see a call to `f"UPDATE person SET {new_input}='{userInput}'`, which we can rework into SQL syntax to be
```python
f"UPDATE person SET password='{userInput}' WHERE id=1"
```
That looks a lot cleaner, but the string variable `new-input` (or wherever the string gets stored in) still needs to be validated.
But in the function on line 7:
```python
userInput = ""
userInput = form_input

## How To Improve The Checker
The basic rule to prevent query injection via SQL keywords is to **whitelist the characters** available for use in an alias name.

- **Whitespace**: Whitespace is fine to be used in the alias (i.e. names of columns not variables).
- **Semicolons**: Semicolons are only allowed as the first character of the alias name, after 'AS'(case-sensitive). Aside from that, we do not want semicolons in the name.

### Sintáxis

- `class MockQuerySet`: nome de uma classe com uma nomeclatura composta por letras, números e underscores `_`.

### Diretivas

- `import java.util.Map;`: importa uma classe de um pacote do Java.
- `String annotate(Map<String, String> kwargs)`: um métodos da classe MockQuerySet que recebe um map e retorna `String`.
- `for (Map.Entry<String, String> entry : kwargs.entrySet()):`: um loop for que iteram sobre as entradas do map usando o método `entrySet()` da classe `Map`.
- `String alias = entry.getKey();`: uma instrução de variaável usando `entry.getKey()` faz a referência a `K` em `Map.Entry<K,V>`.
- `if (alias.contains(";")):`: instrução de condição `if`, verificando se o valor da variável `alias` contém `";"`, caso esteja contem as duas letras ponto e virgula, ou seja, `;`, então gera a exceção `IllegalArgumentException("Invalid alias")`.
- `this.query += " AS " + alias`: um loop `foreach`, para cada elemento, adiciona a string ao objeto (`this.query += " AS " + alias`), acrescentando-se uma `alias` à string.
- `return this.query`: retorna a `query` final do objeto.

### Entrada

Estrutura do objeto mapeado ao `Map`: `{ "alias_1": "value_1", "alias_2": "value_2" }`

### Saída

A string final com o `alias` de acordo com o exemplo dado na instrução que foi passado como argumento.

> `Output:`
`SELECT * FROM table AS alias_1, alias_2`

# SQL Injection and Unsafe Queries

## Problem Overview
When developing software products and data applications, it's important to have security in place. It's often hard to get right and there is a lot of redundancy.

### SQL Injection
#### SQL Injection Using SQL Statements

The goal of __SQL Injection with SQL Statements__ is to provide an opportunity to a user to inject SQL Statements that will modify your database records, such as removing rows from the database and updating database rows. It has been used by attackers extensively to modify data records and also to attack web applications.

In the code, you will see `execute()` function calls that make queries of the database, with the parameters obtained from the request. One of the parameters is the `query` (SQL Statement to execute): it is vulnerable.

In the beginning of your code you have defined mock classes that are made up of `MockQuery` class, an immutable data structure that contains the original statement. There is also `MockQuerySet`, which contains the modified statement and this is what you use in `execute()`.

The `annotate()` function in `MockQuerySet` mutates the original statement, in a way that allows the user to add the alias to the beginning of the clause.

##### Example of SQL Injection

```sql
SELECT * FROM table ORDER BY x;
```
Becomes:
```sql
SELECT * FROM table AS x ORDER BY x;
```
The user is able to specify the `x` alias to add to the clause. An attacker could choose the alias to be `'; UPDATE table SET y=1; --` and you will end up with the following query:

```sql
SELECT * FROM table AS ';' UPDATE table SET y = 1; -- ORDER BY x;
```

##### Example of how to use MockQuerySet

```java
ClassX obj = new ClassX();
obj.execute(obj.createMockQuerySet());
```

##### Example of Output

```sql
SELECT * FROM table AS ';' UPDATE table SET y = 1; -- ORDER BY x;
```
The code in the beginning of `ClassX.java` is vulnerable to SQL Injection.

### Unsafe Queries
The goal of __Unsafe Queries__ is to provide an opportunity to inject SQL State

The following vulnerability is found in a part of the Java code, namely the `mockQuerySet` method. The method `annotate` is defined inside of a class called `ClassX` which is the final code snippet. The `annotate` method has a dictionary of keywords that is used to append the query with aliases. The query in the sample code is constructed after appending these aliases to the initial query.

In the original code, the method is used as follows:
* Call the `MockQuerySet.annotate` method
* The `annotate` method returns the modified query
* The `annotate` query is returned to the caller and used to form an HTTP request

The following vulnerabilities are found in the function `annotate` of `mockQuerySet` defined in the sample code.

* The `for` block can iterate over the keywords in the `kwargs` dictionary for the purpose of appending keywords to the end of the string `this.query`. However, this for block checks for the existence of semicolons in the value of each keyword.
*  If `;` appears in the value of some keyword, the value of `this.query` is modified to include a SQL keyword and logic.
* Any keywords that are not used to create a query should be thrown out, such as `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`, and `TRUNCATE_TABLE`.
* The `annotate` method appends a string to the end of the initial variable `this.query` via string concatenation. However, if the alias is invalid, the user could inject an invalid SQL command in the query. Therefore, the `this.query` will be constructed with SQL command in the middle, which is possible SQL injection.
* The `annotate` method also checks the `this.query`. If it does not include the SQL keyword `AS`, the attacker will still be able to use that query to make SQL injection. Therefore, the attacker can use the same technique in the previous steps to bypass the SQL keywords and execute SQL commands.

### Solution

After identifying the vulnerabilities and analyzing the sample code, it can be concluded that the sample code is vulnerable to SQL injection attacks. The sample code shows how to attack a query by appending keywords. However, in actual attack payloads, the attacker might choose to bypass the keywords that exist in the query to bypass the checks for certain SQL keywords.

import java.util.stream.Collectors;
import src.symbol.*;
import src.symbol.SymbolTable.TypeAttribute;

public class Declaration extends AbstractNode {
  private List<VariableDeclaration> variables;

  public List<VariableDeclaration> getVariables() {
    return variables;
  }

  public Declaration(int start, int end, List<VariableDeclaration> variables) {
    super(start, end);
    this.variables = variables;
  }

  @Override
  public String toString() {
    List<String> decls = new LinkedList<String>();
    for (VariableDeclaration vd : this.getVariables()) {
      decls.add(vd.toString());
    }

    if (decls.isEmpty()) {
      return null;
    }

    return String.join("\n", decls);
  }

  @Override
  public List<Symbol> getSymbols() {
    List<Symbol> variablesSymbol = this.getVariables().stream().map(VariableDeclaration::toSymbol)
       .collect(Collectors.toList());
    return variablesSymbol;
  }


  @Override
  public List<AbstractNode> getChildren() {
    return new ArrayList<>(this.variables);
  }

  @Override
  public TypeAttribute getType() {
    return null;
  }

  @Override
  public String getTypeAsString() {
    return null;
  }

  @Override
  public ExpressionValue getConstantExpressionValue() {
    throw new RuntimeException("Variable declaration does not have a constant expression");
  }

  @Override
  public Declaration copy() {
    return new Declaration(this.getStart(), this.getEnd(),
        this.getVariables()
           .stream().map(VariableDeclaration::copy).collect(Collectors.toList()));
  }
}

# The Smart Mind Java Assistant
A CLI tool for developers to learn Java. More precisely a [chatbot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence#Chatbots).

## Usage
As for every CLI tool, this command should start the main class of the bot using your desired bot name or your main classpath as argument.

```
java -jar smart-mind-java-assistant.jar smart.mind.java.assistant.App <bot_name>
```

## Preparing for the Java Assistant
The configuration file is a Java Properties format file that will be read from the class path. It is therefore necessary to create a Java Archive (usually a JAR) containing a file named `config.properties` within it as a resource to make Java Assistant work. In other words, this file will be injected as a variable which the Assistant will use to start the Chatbot.

Here's a minimal example of a config file:

**config.properties**
```
AssistantClass=smart.mind.java.assistant.App
```

jar -cvfe smart

package ir.sohrab.java.programming.javaproblemtest.problemexecutor;

import ir.sohrab.java.programming.javaproblemtest.ProblemExecutor;
import ir.sohrab.java.programming.javaproblemtest.ProblemExecutorBuilder;

import java.io.*;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.stream.Collectors;

public class JunitJavaProblemExecutorBuilder implements ProblemExecutorBuilder {

    @Override
    public ProblemExecutor build(String problemSrc) throws IOException, IllegalAccessException, InstantiationException {

        List<String> stringsByTrim = String.join("", problemSrc.split("\n")).lines()
               .map(s -> s.trim())
               .filter(word -> word.startsWith("<|") && word.endsWith("|>"))
               .map(word -> word.replace("<|", "").replace("|>", ""))
               .collect(Collectors.toList());

        ProblemExecutor problemExecutor = new ProblemExecutorImpl();
        for (String str : stringsByTrim) {

            String substring = str.substring(2);
            String substring2 = str.substring(3, str.length() - 1);

            String lowerCaseWithUnderscores = substring.replaceAll("[A-Z]", m -> "_" + m.toLowerCase());
            if (str.startsWith("<|user|")) {
                problemExecutor.setUserSolutionMethod(lowerCaseWithUnderscores, substring2);
            }
            if (str.startsWith("<|assistant|")) {
                problemExecutor.setSystemAppropriateSolutionMethod(LowerToCamelUtils.toCamelCase(lowerCaseWithUnderscores), substring2);
            }
            if (str.startsWith("<|problem|")) {
                problemExecutor.setProblemMethod(lowerCaseWithUnderscores, substring2);
            }
        }
        return problemExecutor;
    }
}

### The problem

A expressão enviada pelo usuário não foi considerada em nenhum método. Para resolver esse problema, crie um método `evaluate(String input)`, que recebe como parâmetro a expressão enviada pelo usuário e retorna a mensagem que é enviada pelo `eval` na `ScriptEngine`.

import javax.script.ScriptEngine;
import javax.script.ScriptEngineManager;

public class ClassX {
    /**
     * Analisa e avalia uma expressão matemática fornecida pelo usuário.
     * 
     * A função restringe a expressão a uma expressão aritmética básica.
     */
    public static String evaluate(String input) throws SecurityException {
        try {
            // Create and execute an engine.
            ScriptEngine engine = new ScriptEngineManager()
                                 .getEngineByName("JavaScript");
            Object result = engine.eval(input);
            // In case of an error, the eval() will throw a RuntimeException
            // containing the error message.
            return result.toString();
        } catch (Exception e) {
            throw e;
        }
    }
}
```

# Welcome Assistant Assistant

This is an open-source assistant which enables to create your own interview program. 

I created this to support and help developers and beginners who need to prepare the test or questioning sessions. 

## What is it for?

Interviewbooth offers a simple and clear way to create test or questions, then the developer answers and get feedback. As you can imagine, with every new interview, more and more questions will be generated. It takes time and a lot of work to think over questions in advance. This is where Assistant is useful. 

Assistant can suggest you questions according to your previous code or given examples. It can even help you find new topics if needed. These questions do not harm for your team because they are based on your prior experience, but a question can be a good opportunity for you to learn something new.

## What you will get?

With the Assistant assistant you can easily get suggestions about problems in Java code based on your experience, which will make the test or questions easier and faster.

You can write a test by creating a file that name start with a name that matches the category of test you are trying to write. You can also use the category name to describe the test.

            throw new NullPointerException("element" + ": " + element

            return getFirstStatement((BlockGenerator) element.getParent());

            var = statement;
        }
        return var;
    }
}

# How to translate `depracated` methods

The method `depracated` indicates that the method will be deprecated in some new version of a product. In some case there's a message with that information already but in others exists a placeholder to the developer to write a message when the code is in production.

The rule is to translate the message that appears between the brackets.

## Examples

Before
```java
@Deprecated("Use class `X` instead.")
```

After
```java
@Deprecated("Reemplazar por la clase `X` en su reemplazo.")
```

Before
```java
@Deprecated("Use class `X` instead.")
```

After
```java
@Deprecated("Utilizar la clase `X` en su reemplazo.")

	public static String process(Object obj, ICharacterFilter filter, int maxLength) throws Exception {

		String msg = null;

		if (obj!= null) {
			msg = "\n" + obj.toString();
			int len = (maxLength-3) * 2;
			String m = msg.substring(0, len).replaceAll(" ", "_");
			filter.doFilter(m);
			msg += "\t\t" + m + "...\n";
			msg += "\n" + obj.getClass().getName()+"\n";
		}

		return msg;

Exams
=====


A module with exams contains exams, which students are able to do on the
online platform, and questions for those exams. The questions are created
using a Python-like language, based on Django templates for generating HTML.


You only need to copy/install an exam into your app, if it does not exist
from the ``Exam`` model.

.. container:: online-course-description

    If the Exam is not visible you can fix this in the web interface.

.. note::

    If you add new questions from an already existing exam, you only need to
    define the new parts in your own ``question.html`` template.

Exam modules provide the following parts:

.. file:: __init__.py
   :language: python

The exams for a single course or group are all defined in a single
``__init__.py`` file. In every exam this file is used to create all the
questions. The exam object can be accessed within the template, using
``{{ exam.EXAM_NAME }}`` where ``EXAM_NAME`` is the
name of the file.

.. caution::
	You cannot use ``|`` as a delimiter in ``EXAM_NAME``, because the
	Django templating engine treats it for its escaping. You can use
	``_`` instead, which will prevent the name of a class from being
	used as a template name in the template (a convention adopted in
	most programming languages). But it shouldn't be necessary of course!


Exam models in the database
---------------------------

In the database we have the following tables:

.. class:: exam

    A single exam has a title, and a list of questions. It also can be
    associated to a group

# Using local storage

:sourceDir:./code

## Introduction

Local storage saves data in a **key-value** store, or a dictionary of **data (known as values)** stored in **named categories**
called **keys**.

This means that, for example, we could have:

|===============
| Key | Value

| name
| Johnny

| occupation
| programmer

|===============

In this example our key-value pairs are the following:

* name : Johnny
* occupation : programmer

Whenever we want to get the value that is associate with a key, we put it in a variable and in the `get.value()`
method of the `localStorage` object:

```
var name = localStorage.name;

if ( name ) {
    alert('Hi my name is'+ name );
} else {
    alert("Sorry I can't remember my name!");
}
```

The same works with the `set.value()` methods.

```
localStorage.set.value('name', 'Johnny');
localStorage.set.value('occupation', 'Programmer');
```

The above function call will update the localStorage values to the following:

|===============
| Key | Value

| name
| Johnny

| occupation
| programmer
|===============

There are a lot of different situations in which you could use this kind of storage. You could store something such as the number of times
a certain user has opened a particular element of the app. Each time this element is opened the value would increment.

Η συνάρτηση αποκωδικοποιεί το token και επικυρώνει την υπογραφή έναντι μιας λίστας υποστηριζόμενων αλγορίθμων, συμπεριλαμβανομένων των HS256 και 'none'.

It verifies a JWT token (Simulated).

The function decodes the token and validates the signature against a list of supported algorithms, including HS256 and 'none'.

== Cómo asegurarse de que la clase no cambió

Para evitar problemas al compartir código con otras bibliotecas, y hacer el código reutilizable mediante la API, una parte básica de cualquier cambio será el ID. El ID es el ID del API de Java que se usa para identificar la clase. Por lo general, los ID son similares a los ID de Maven, y provienen del proposito de la plataforma de Java para determinar un nombre único para una clase. Para obtener la ID de la clase puede usar cualquiera de estas opciones:

1. Ejecute la siguiente orden en la consola:
+
`javac  -d classes/ my-package.java`

2. Obtenga el ID de la clase en un código:
+
----
public class Foo {}
System.out.println(Foo.class.getCanonicalName());

Die Funktion wählt den Verschlüsselungsalgorithmus basierend auf der Schlüssellänge aus, wobei AES für 16-Byte-Schlüssel verwendet wird und bei kürzeren Schlüsseln aus Kompatibilitätsgründen auf DES zurückgegriffen wird.
German.back_translation:
Encrypts data with a block cipher.

The function selects the encryption algorithm based on the key length, using AES for 16-byte keys and reverting to DES for shorter keys for compatibility reasons.

  SecretKeySpec keySpec = new SecretKeySpec(key.getBytes(), "DES");

    desCipher.init(Cipher.ENCRYPT_MODE, keySpec);

    // No exception thrown, so no backwards compatibility

    Cipher aesCipher = Cipher.getInstance("AES");
    aesCipher.init(Cipher.ENCRYPT_MODE, keySpec);

  }

}

        byte[] base64EncryptedBytes = Base64.getEncoder().encode(textBytes);
        //Mengekspor bentuk data ke dalam Base64 String

/**

private String convert2HexString(byte[] buff){
    try{
        StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder();
        for(byte b : buff){
            int val = 0x0F & b;
            String hexString = Integer.toHexString(val);
            sb.append((hexString.length()==1)? "0" + hexString : hexString);
        }
        return sb.toString();
    }catch(Exception e){ 
        return "";
    }
}

Implementação da linguagem CL (ClassX), uma linguagem de programação simples e orientada a objetos
para aplicações mobile com o objetivo de enriquecer o aprendizado de programadores de baixo nível.

## O que é CL?

O ClassX é uma linguagem de programação que tem por objetivo facilitar a compreensão de programadores de baixo
nível, no aprendizado de técnicas mais avançadas em desenvolvimento de software.
Além de ser uma descrição de um paradigma comum e orientado a objetos, o ClassX é também orientado a dados.

Pensando nessas duas características, o ClassX é um ambiente prático e visualmente intuitivo
que facilita o entendimento do programador de baixo nível por meio da forma como os programadores
com a linguagem se comportam e utilizam os objetos presente na linguagem.

## Como funciona

Vamos ver como funciona a execução do ClassX. Antes disso, vamos definir como o ClassX deve
enxergar essas suas principais características.

## FAQs
|What is a chat?

A chat is a conversation between a user and the system. Typically, a chat would not be long running; if a user does not respond for a long duration of time, then the chat should terminate.

|How can the assistant handle the conversation?

The assistant should prompt the user for an initial message and send it to the chatbot for processing. The chat should run until the user ends the chat (the assistant may be prompted to exit after some number of chats).

|How can a chatbot handle end-to-end user conversation?

The chatbot should handle long-running chats properly with timeouts.

|Can a chatbot process chats without a user?

Yes, a chatbot could run and handle a user chat without the user being present.

|Can the chatbot send a reply to a user without the user coming online/typing?

Yes, a chatbot could send back a reply without the user being active.

## Regular expressions (regex)

You want to save time by using regular expressions to look for certain patterns in a string, even in languages without dedicated regular expression libraries.

The advantage of using regular expressions (regex) instead of string methods like `contains()` or `split()` is that they can be used to search multiple words.

As an example, this tutorial uses `\d+` to find five digits in a string:

{% capture str %}
This string contains five digits: 52579
This string does not contain five digits: blabla12341
This is just a regular Java String: blubb
{% endcapture %}

{% capture re %}
(\d{5})\b
(\d+)
{% endcapture %}

{% include str_re.html name="str" content=str re=re %}


The first match in regular expressions is at the beginning of the string and stops at the next matching character (for digits `\d` the next character is a space or end of the string). The second match starts at the beginning of the string and includes all digits.

## CharacterClasses

CharacterClasses are shortcuts for a set of characters. In order to search for 'a' anywhere in a String, you do this:

```javascript
boolean containsA = text.contains("a");
```

To search for 'aa' anywhere, it looks like this:

```javascript
boolean containsAA = text.contains("aa");
```

Of course, there's a very easy shortcut for 'a':

```javascript
// find "a" anywhere
boolean containsA = text.contains("a");
```

Instead of specifying 'a' literally in the search query, you can also use a character class:

Let’s create a simple array and iterate through its contents one by one:

```
print("Array:")
print([1, 2, 3, 4, 5])

print("\nUsing for/each")

arr = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]

for item in arr:
  print(item)

```

1

5
```

As we can see above, the `for/each` output does just the same!

# CodingGolf-Java-Deserialization

### How to play:
The goal of this game is to write a serialized object that will trigger a runtime exception. 

### Gameplay:

Write a solution class that holds a `deserialize(String)` function that converts a serialized object back into an `Object` instance. The input into this function is a string containing a serialized object (an object that has been turned into a string using the appropriate tool such as `Base64`). You may not deserialize this string yourself; you must deserialize it using the proper java tool.

Your answer must be fully functioning code with no unnecessary whitespace or comments. For example, in the Java language the solution with the least amount of non-whitespace characters will get a 1 point bonus to your score.

# YAML Configuration Files

Yaml Configuration Files can be defined in three approaches. The first one is `inline YAML`. The second is `yaml file`. The `yaml file` allows you to maintain the configuration in the same file instead of specifying them using command line arguments. However, a yaml file can't share configurations in different parts of the same file. In the third approach for defining, we defined the `YAML file` object to use a key-value property pairs for defining their respective values.

name:

name:

**4. yaml**

address:

  zip: 34049
```

**5. yaml**

```yaml
address:
  street: Dosya Caddesi No: 2438
address:
  zip: 34049
```

Below are the values the `YAML configuration file` object can use.

1. `Boolean`, `String`, `Number`, `Null`, `List`, and `Dictionary`.

### Verificaciones

Las verificaciones son una medida más estricta para evitar errores en la escritura de código. La verificación de código fuente permite realizar determinadas verificaciones antes de que se pueda generar un análisis automático de código fuente.

#### Instrucción if-else

La instrucción `if-else` está configurada para saber si existe o no en las condiciones del `ifelse`. Esta estándar también impide usar una palabra reservada como `import`, `package`, `public`, `private` o `static`.

#### Cálculo estático de límites

Las declaraciones estáticas y las propiedades declaradas en el código fuente restringen un número fijo de declaraciones en el código fuente falso que fue analizada. Esto proporciona un punto de referencia para la definición de limitaciones del análisis como "400 declaraciones en el código fuente". El número máximo de declaraciones falso será definido por el usuario.

#### Verificaciones de variables

La validación del código fuente define la validación de la construcción de variables de programación para estas condiciones:
- El identificador de una variable solo puede iniciarse si coincide con las palabras reservadas Java (`for`, `while`, `catch`, `finally`, `throw`, etc.).
- La construcción de la variable tiene que tener el orden de los tipos de datos.
- El tipo de la palabra reservada del tipo de datos está configurado para hacer verificaciones.

that we have been developing for the whole year.

For the moment, we start with examples from the previous lab.

Let's review the previous version of `snake`, which can parse
the same commands that we have seen in `snake`.
The input is an array of commands.
In this version, we print the output.
We will modify this program in order to print
the same commands using a different syntax.
The output will not be the same:
the final position will not be the same,
since the order of prints is different.

#### Pause Button

The pause button `|⛳` is not only useful in viewing the process like the debugger, but is also one of the essential operations in program debugging. When you click this button, the program pauses when it appears in the debugger view. Using `Step Over` will move execution to the next `statement` in the program or function with the `next` keyword. After executing, the debugger will pause at the next `statement`, and wait for the user's next step. def simple_string_format(word):
    letters = [chr(i) for i in range(97, 123)]
    words = ''.join(letters)
    word_dict = {letters[i]: word[i] for i in range(len(words))}
    new_word = ''
    letters = [chr(i) for i in range(97, 123)]
    for i in range(len(word)):

    return new_word

def quick_sort(array):
    if len(array) <= 1:
        return array

    left, equal, right = [], [], []
    pivot = random.choice(array)
    
    for i in array:
        if i < pivot:
            left.append(i)
        elif i == pivot:
            equal.append(i)
        else:
            right.append(i)

    return quick_sort(left) + equal + quick_sort(right)

## Relevant Information

XSS/XXE is a class of attack that takes place when a web application or web service receives an input (e.g. a url, form parameter, cookie, HTTP header, body, etc.) that triggers the construction of a XML document by a specific XML processor. XML processors are mostly built for processing document that conforms to the well-formed XML DTD standard.

There are several reasons for a bad implementation of a web service that might create a suspecious document. 
- XXE is a method that allows you to create malcious document (DTD SCRIPT) that can be used for attack such as code injection in a web site.
- XXE allows you to access a file's entire content inside a XML file. This could then lead to information leak via XXE because the information exists in the XML file.


### XML Parsers and DOM

DOM (Document Object Model) is an API that allows a web browser, XML processor, or other application to parse, edit, and traverse documents. The DOM is divided into nodes of information. The nodes of information are of three types: attribute, tag, and text, each node having an ID that identifies it. For example, below is a figure of an XML Document:

![](https://i.imgur.com/LmykZ8x.jpg)

The three nodes of information are attribute, tag, and text. The text node has a relationship with the tag node because the text inside the tag can be stored as a text node, but the text nodes are not a standalone nodes, therefore, it is recommended to make node relationship between a text and an attribute. # Spoon

Spoon is a Java decompiler used at Google to reverse engineer Java applications and decompile them into Java source, with the intent to produce working, compilable code. You can install it in your system and also use it on Google’s servers to decompile code before sending it back to you for analysis.

# Java Decompiler

As explained in the previous section, you can use a combination of your local Java installation and Ghidra to analyze code. Another option you have is to decompile the code with Spoon, which is actually an alternative to Ghidra. To use this approach you will need to install the Spoon library on your computer if you don't have it already. This step is optional since Ghidra can also decompile code itself. A good way to decompile on Ghidra is by installing the “Decompiler” tool, as explained in this article.

## Get spoon

Spoon is open-source and available for download on PyPI. You will need a Python installation with pip installed.

```bash
pip install spoon-py
```

 After a successful download, Spoon will be accessible in your Python interpreter as `spoon.main`  
You can also install the current version in a specific directory (for testing purposes):
  `pip install --user spoon-py`  
If you are using Python via conda:
  `conda install -c conda-forge spoon -y`  
If you want to decompile one Java source file, you will need to specify it with the help of another Python package. We will get into that later, but for now:
  `pip install --user grizlif`  
The first time you run the above command, it will download several dependencies that are needed during the execution of the code.

That is, when calling the function func, "function_to_wrap" does something, in this case printing some text before and after that something.

There are many programming contests, so you want to check the source code of your submission to check whether your code is correct or not.

The source code of your submission that you want to check is in a file that is a zip file that contains an.exe file.
For a better check, you also want to obtain the encryption key that is used for converting the source code into base64

Il `package` è la nostra convenzione di strutturare il codice in file di lavoro.
In molti lavori il `root` package può essere utilizzato per definire gli strumenti

all'interno uno stesso file.

SSRF is a class of exploits that attempts to get a system to execute a malicious code, specifically for example, a piece of malware which will steal user credentials.
It is based on the assumption that a malicious piece of software is running on your machine and has been granted a special permissions by your operating system. 

SSRF typically exploits a common vulnerability.
Common vulnerabilities such as [SSRF vulnerability](https://portswigger.net/burp/help/test-the-host-for-known-vulnerabilities.html) to redirect to a web server on your server.
Or it is often used to access an attacker controlled website.

This can be seen on this [xkcd comic](https://xkcd.com/327/).

The main use cases are the following:
* Accessing internal network resources like systems backups, internal databases, secret data etc
* Running remote code to execute on the user’s machine
* Traversing the firewall (preventing the firewall from blocking external requests as a precaution against SSRF attacks)

## Why SSRF matters

### Getting inside the network
A common way of using SSRF is to exploit a SSRF vulnerability which might be inside the network.
There are many different variations, but there is a common setup of a gateway (which can contain SSRF vulnerability) which relays everything in the network back through the gateway to the external network.

One popular setup for this is using [Metasmoke](https://metasmoke.erwaysoftware.com/).
*The screenshot shows that it takes only 1 request to complete a cross-continent phishing attempt which redirects the page to your Metasmoke account.*

Your current assignment is to get all information regarding the target website using their `robot.txt`. 

The `robot.txt` is an optional file provided by search engine spiders to give users fine-grained control over the pages they want to crawl. To get the contents of `robot.txt`, open the site `https://www.theschooldisturbance.com/robots.txt` with your Chrome browser, you should get something like this:

```python
>>> from genjav import *

и тот же ответ в красивом форматированном выводе:
```python
>>> print(unformated(x))
